key_insight: Code can serve not just as LLM output but as an operational "agent harness": a reusable, executable substrate that encodes reasoning, actions, environment models, and verification loops to make agentic systems more reliable and interpretable.
problem_solved: Addresses brittleness and poor verifiability of agentic LLM systems by providing a concrete, software-engineering‑style way to integrate generation, execution, and testing into agent loops.
method: Introduce the "agent harness" framing and taxonomy that treats code as the medium for agent reasoning, acting, environment modeling, and execution-based checks.

Provide design patterns and implementation recipes (scaffolded code templates, execution-test-refine loops, modular environment interfaces) that let LLMs generate and interact with executable harnesses.
Validate the approach with prototypes and usage scenarios that demonstrate improved interpretability, modularity, and execution-driven verification (generation → run → test → refine).
impact: Makes building LLM-driven agents more engineering-friendly: easier to debug, verify, and iterate by treating code as the canonical artifact for reasoning and execution. This bridges ML capabilities with software-engineering practices for safer, more reliable agents.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: LLM ↔ Code Harness ↔ Environment showing bidirectional flow (generate code → execute → observe → refine).
Flowchart of the execution-based loop: generate code → run in sandbox → run tests/validators → feed results back to model.
Before/After comparison: conventional prompts-only agent vs. code-as-harness agent, highlighting verifiability and modularity gains.
Annotated code snippet + execution trace illustrating how a generated harness encodes actions, checks, and environment models.
paper_authors: Xuying Ning, Katherine Tieu, Dongqi Fu, Tianxin Wei, Zihao Li
